# Squared-Xi polynomial--Gaussian Weil disproof family

- **ID:** `squared-xi-polynomial-gaussian-weil-disproof`
- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Type:** THEOREM / RH-COMPLETE FILTERED HEAT SOURCE REDUCTION
- **Scientific status:** `[PAPER COMPLETE CRITERION] [FILTERED ENDPOINT LEAN-FORMALIZED] [COMPLETENESS LEAN OPEN] [NO NEGATIVE SOURCE VALUE YET]`
- **Parent:** `squared-xi-parabolic-heat-trace-disproof.md`
- **Statement:** RH is equivalent to nonnegativity of every polynomial-square Gaussian trace on
  the multiplicity-exact squared centered Xi divisor.  If RH is false, one real polynomial cancels
  the entire lower finite packet and the Gaussian suppresses the remaining tail, producing a
  strict negative finite differential expression in the completed Gaussian prime/Gamma source.

## 1. Filtered heat trace

For each multiplicity copy `q`, put

```text
z_q=(rho_q-1/2)*(-i),       u_q=z_q^2.                    (1)
```

For `t>0` and `P in R[U]`, define

```text
H_(P,t)=sum_q P(u_q)^2*exp(-t*u_q).                      (2)
```

The existing unconditional strip and height estimates give the uniform sector

```text
Re(u_q) > |z_q|^2/2 > 0.                                 (3)
```

Consequently every series `(2)` is absolutely summable: polynomial growth is absorbed by half
of the Gaussian, and the other half is dominated by the already summable divisor
`sum_q |z_q|^(-2)`.

Critical-line reflection sends `u_q` to `conj(u_q)`.  Since `P` has real coefficients, `(2)` is
real unconditionally.

## 2. RH-positive direction

Under RH every `z_q` is a nonzero real number, hence every `u_q` is positive real.  Termwise,

```text
P(u_q)^2*exp(-t*u_q) >= 0,                               (4)
```

so `H_(P,t)>=0` for every real polynomial and every positive time.

Thus one strict negative value in `(2)` proves `not RiemannHypothesis`.

## 3. Completeness: every off-line orbit has a negative filtered heat witness

Assume RH is false and select a nonreal centered spectral point `alpha`.  Because its real part is
the nonzero zero ordinate and its imaginary part is the transverse displacement,

```text
u_0=alpha^2
```

is nonreal.  Let `A_0=Re(u_0)`.

By `(3)` and reciprocal-square summability, only finitely many distinct squared divisor values
have real part at most `A_0+1`.  Choose `delta>0` so that the finite conjugation-closed packet

```text
S={u_q : Re(u_q)<=A_0+delta}                             (5)
```

contains `u_0,conj(u_0)` and has no value with real part strictly between the boundary of `S` and
`A_0+delta`.

For each `t>0`, real Lagrange interpolation on the conjugation-closed set `S` gives
`P_t in R[U]` with

```text
P_t(u_0)= i*exp(t*u_0/2),
P_t(conj(u_0))=conj(P_t(u_0)),
P_t(u)=0                    for u in S\{u_0,conj(u_0)}.  (6)
```

Every divisor copy above `u_0` or its conjugate then contributes exactly `-1` to `(2)`, while all
other copies in `S` contribute zero.

The Lagrange basis is fixed.  Hence there are constants `C,d`, independent of `t`, such that

```text
|P_t(u)| <= C*exp(t*A_0/2)*(1+|u|)^d.                    (7)
```

Outside `S`, `Re(u)>=A_0+delta`.  Combining `(3)` and `(7)` gives, for `t>=1`,

```text
|P_t(u_q)^2*exp(-t*u_q)|
 <= C^2*(1+|u_q|)^(2d)*exp(-t*(Re(u_q)-A_0)).            (8)
```

After one half of the gap `delta` is extracted, the remaining exponential is bounded by a
constant multiple of `|z_q|^(-2)`.  Dominated convergence and reciprocal-square summability show
that the tail in `(8)` tends to zero as `t->infinity`.

The finite packet contributes a fixed negative integer and the tail tends to zero.  Therefore

```text
exists t>0, exists P in R[U], H_(P,t)<0.                 (9)
```

This proves the exact criterion

```text
RiemannHypothesis
  <-> forall t>0, forall P in R[U], 0<=H_(P,t).          (10)
```

Strict negativity is open in `t` and in the finitely many coefficients.  Rational approximation
therefore reduces the disproof family to positive rational times and rational polynomials.

Lean now formalizes unconditional polynomial-weighted Gaussian summability, Schwarz reality, the
RH-positive direction, and the strict-negative RH-false endpoint in
`RHTower/XiGaussianHeatTraceDisproof.lean`.  The interpolation-plus-tail completeness direction is
still paper-only.

## 4. Completed source differential

Write

```text
P(U)^2=sum_(j=0)^D a_j U^j.                              (11)
```

Absolute convergence permits termwise heat differentiation, giving

```text
H_(P,t)=sum_(j=0)^D a_j*(-1)^j*d^j/dt^j Theta_Xi(t).    (12)
```

/-!
# The finite-polynomial source contour and its exact residue

Transport preserves the negative spectral contribution. The right-line
real integral has a bound independent of Gaussian width, for every finite
real coefficient vector and every full-positive source.
-/

open Complex MeasureTheory Filter Topology Set
open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower.WeilSingularArithmetic

open GaussZeroSum

theorem integrable_sourceZetaPairing_finite_right {lam : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {T : ℝ} (hT : 1 ≤ T) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => sourceZetaPairing hW ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      gaussWeight T ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      sourceFiniteWeight N c ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I)) := by
  simpa only [Complex.ofReal_div, Complex.ofReal_ofNat] using
    integrable_mul_sourceFiniteWeight (integrable_sourceZetaPairing_gaussian_right hW hT)
      N c (σ := 3 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)

/-- The pole contribution survives polynomial weighting with its exact coefficient. -/
theorem sourceZetaPairing_finite_shift {lam : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {T : ℝ} (hT : 1 ≤ T) :
    (∫ t : ℝ, sourceZetaPairing hW ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      gaussWeight T ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      sourceFiniteWeight N c ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I)) -
    (∫ t : ℝ, sourceZetaPairing hW ((3 / 4 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      gaussWeight T ((3 / 4 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      sourceFiniteWeight N c ((3 / 4 : ℂ) + t * I)) =
      -(Real.pi : ℂ) * sourcePoleNumerator hW 1 * gaussWeight T 1 * sourceFiniteWeight N c 1 := by
  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := exists_sourceZetaPairing_gaussian_tail_decay hW hT
  obtain ⟨B, hB0, hB⟩ := exists_sourceFiniteWeight_strip_bound N c
  have hb (s : ℂ) (hs0 : 3 / 4 ≤ s.re) (hs1 : s.re ≤ 3 / 2) (ht : 2 ≤ |s.im|) :
      ‖sourceZetaPairing hW s * gaussWeight T s * sourceFiniteWeight N c s‖ ≤
        A * B * (1 + s.im ^ 2)⁻¹ := by
    rw [norm_mul]
    calc
      _ ≤ ‖sourceZetaPairing hW s * gaussWeight T s‖ * B :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hB s (by linarith) hs1) (norm_nonneg _)
      _ ≤ (A * (1 + s.im ^ 2)⁻¹) * B :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hA s hs0 hs1 ht) hB0
      _ = _ := by ring
  have hr := ((tendsto_mul_sourceZetaPairing hW).mul
    ((differentiable_gaussWeight T 1).continuousAt.tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds)).mul
      ((differentiable_sourceFiniteWeight N c 1).continuousAt.tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds)
  have hr' : Tendsto (fun s => (s - 1) *
      (sourceZetaPairing hW s * gaussWeight T s * sourceFiniteWeight N c s)) (𝓝[≠] 1)
      (𝓝 ((-sourcePoleNumerator hW 1 / 2) * gaussWeight T 1 * sourceFiniteWeight N c 1)) := by
    simpa only [mul_assoc] using hr
  have hs := integral_line_sub_integral_line_eq
    (F := fun s => sourceZetaPairing hW s * gaussWeight T s * sourceFiniteWeight N c s)
    (a := 3 / 4) (b := 3 / 2) (p := 1) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
    (fun s hs0 _ hs1 => ((differentiableAt_sourceZetaPairing hW (by linarith) hs1).mul
      (differentiable_gaussWeight T s)).mul (differentiable_sourceFiniteWeight N c s)) hr' hb
  push_cast at hs
  convert hs using 1
  ring

/-- Explicit pole budget, uniform in width, finite length, and coefficients. -/
theorem re_integral_sourceZetaPairing_finite_right_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {T : ℝ} (hT : 1 ≤ T) :
    (∫ t : ℝ, sourceZetaPairing hW ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      gaussWeight T ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I) *
      sourceFiniteWeight N c ((3 / 2 : ℂ) + t * I)).re ≤
        Real.pi * ‖sourcePoleNumerator hW 1‖ * Real.exp (1 / 4) *
          ‖sourceFiniteWeight N c 1‖ := by
  have hs := congrArg Complex.re (sourceZetaPairing_finite_shift hW N c hT)
  rw [Complex.sub_re] at hs
  have hleft := re_integral_sourceZetaPairing_finite_nonpos hW N c hT
  have hg : gaussWeight T 1 = ((Real.exp (1 / (4 * T ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
    unfold gaussWeight
    rw [Complex.ofReal_exp]
    congr 1

The canonical real pairing vanishes. The actual Herglotz pairing is a

theorem integrable_mul_sourceFiniteWeight {v : ℝ → ℂ} (hv : Integrable v)
    (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ0 : 1 / 4 ≤ σ) (hσ1 : σ ≤ 3 / 2) :
    Integrable (fun t : ℝ => v t * sourceFiniteWeight N c ((σ : ℂ) + t * I)) := by
  obtain ⟨B, _, hB⟩ := exists_sourceFiniteWeight_strip_bound N c
  have hc : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => sourceFiniteWeight N c ((σ : ℂ) + t * I)) :=
    (differentiable_sourceFiniteWeight N c).continuous.comp (by fun_prop)
  exact hv.mul_bdd hc.aestronglyMeasurable (Eventually.of_forall fun t =>
    hB _ (by simpa using hσ0) (by simpa using hσ1))

theorem exists_zetaGaussian_finite_decay (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {T : ℝ} (hT : 1 ≤ T) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 4 ≤ s.re → s.re ≤ 3 / 4 →
      ‖zetaGaussianPairingTest T s * sourceFiniteWeight N c s‖ * (1 + s.im ^ 2) ^ 2 ≤ C := by
  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := exists_zetaGaussianPairingTest_decay hT
  obtain ⟨B, hB0, hB⟩ := exists_sourceFiniteWeight_strip_bound N c
  refine ⟨B * A, fun s hs0 hs1 => ?_⟩

    _ ≤ ‖zetaGaussianPairingTest T s‖ * B * (1 + s.im ^ 2) ^ 2 := by
      gcongr
      exact hB s hs0 (by linarith)
    _ = B * (‖zetaGaussianPairingTest T s‖ * (1 + s.im ^ 2) ^ 2) := by ring
    _ ≤ _ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hA s hs0 hs1) hB0

      Complex.im_ofNat, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, mul_zero, zero_mul,
      add_zero, sub_zero]

        C * K * sourceFiniteEnergy N c * ((N : ℝ) + 1) ^ (9 / 8 : ℝ) * T ^ (5 / 6 : ℝ) :=

theorem exists_re_sourceFiniteGaussianSum_growing_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ}

  obtain ⟨D, hD0, hD⟩ := exists_re_sourceFiniteGaussianSum_energy_le hW

  have hT0 : 0 < T := by linarith
  have hE : 0 ≤ sourceFiniteEnergy N c := Finset.sum_nonneg fun m _ => by positivity

    _ ≤ D * sourceFiniteEnergy N c * ((N : ℝ) + 1) ^ (9 / 8 : ℝ) * T ^ (5 / 6 : ℝ) :=

/-- Every polynomial theta-pair correlation is absolutely integrable. -/
theorem integrable_cusp_correlation (R Q : ℝ[X]) (y : ℝ) :
    Integrable (fun u => cuspSeries R u * cuspSeries Q (y - u)) := by
  simp_rw [cuspSeries_eq_sum_monomials R, cuspSeries_eq_sum_monomials Q,
    Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
  refine integrable_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => ?_)
  refine integrable_finsetSum _ (fun l _ => ?_)
  refine ((integrable_monomial_correlation j l y).const_mul (R.coeff j * Q.coeff l)).congr
    (ae_of_all _ fun u => ?_)
  dsimp only
  ring

/-- Full polynomial theta-pair/divisor--Bessel identity.  No finite theta truncation is used. -/
theorem cusp_correlation_bessel (R Q : ℝ[X]) (y : ℝ) :
    (∫ u, cuspSeries R u * cuspSeries Q (y - u)) =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (R.natDegree + 1), ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (Q.natDegree + 1),
        R.coeff j * Q.coeff l *
          (∑' N : ℕ, (N.divisorsAntidiagonal.card : ℝ) * besselMonomial j l y N) := by
  have hint (j l : ℕ) : Integrable (fun u =>
      (R.coeff j * cuspSeries (X ^ j) u) * (Q.coeff l * cuspSeries (X ^ l) (y - u))) := by
    convert (integrable_monomial_correlation j l y).const_mul (R.coeff j * Q.coeff l) using 1
    ext u
    ring
  simp_rw [cuspSeries_eq_sum_monomials R, cuspSeries_eq_sum_monomials Q,
    Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => integrable_finsetSum _ (fun l _ => hint j l))]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j _
  rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun l _ => hint j l)]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro l _
  calc
    _ = R.coeff j * Q.coeff l * ∫ u, cuspSeries (X ^ j) u * cuspSeries (X ^ l) (y - u) := by
      rw [← integral_const_mul]
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards with u
      ring
    _ = _ := by rw [monomial_correlation_bessel]

/-- Exact actual derivative-correlation matrix, including mixed orders and every divisor term.
In particular, `k=l` and `y=log n` gives the matrix in conjecture C11. -/
theorem derivative_correlation_bessel (k l : ℕ) (y : ℝ) :
    (∫ u, (riemannKernelDeriv k u).re * (riemannKernelDeriv l (u - y)).re) =
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ l *
        (∑ j ∈ Finset.range ((riemannKernelPoly k).natDegree + 1),
          ∑ m ∈ Finset.range ((riemannKernelPoly l).natDegree + 1),
            (riemannKernelPoly k).coeff j * (riemannKernelPoly l).coeff m *
              (∑' N : ℕ, (N.divisorsAntidiagonal.card : ℝ) * besselMonomial j m y N)) := by
  rw [← cusp_correlation_bessel]
  rw [← integral_const_mul]
  apply integral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards with u
  rw [show u - y = -(y - u) by ring, kernelDeriv_re_reflect]
  simp only [riemannKernelDeriv, riemannKernelPoly, Complex.ofReal_re]

/-!
# The restricted Weil eigenproblem: a square Evans determinant

Four exact mechanisms of the card are formalized.

*Equal dimensions.*  The characteristic source `F_{a,λ}` and the Bessel residual target
`R_{a,λ}` both have dimension `d_{a,λ} = 2L_{a,λ}`, so the Evans map `(7)` is **square** — this is
`(3)`–`(4)`.

*Kernel transfer.*  Under the isomorphism `(8)` the eigenspace is trivial exactly when the Evans
kernel is trivial.

*The determinant criterion.*  A square matrix has vanishing determinant exactly when its kernel is
nontrivial, so `(9)`: `λ ∈ spec(A_a) ⟺ det N_{a,λ} = 0`.

*The parity grading.*  The reflection splitting `(22)` adds the two equal halves to the full
dimension, so no excess parity channel occurs.

The restricted Weil form, the Paley–Wiener compression `(12)`, the logarithmic Dirichlet
reconstruction `(5)` and the residual computation `(6)` are cited parents and stay outside the Lean
statement.
-/

open Matrix

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-! ## Equal dimensions -/

/-- **Equations (3)–(4).**  Source and target of the Evans map have the same dimension, so the map
is square. -/
theorem finrank_source_eq_target {p : Polynomial ℂ} {L : ℕ} (hp : p ≠ 0)
    (hdeg : p.natDegree = 2 * L) :
    Module.finrank ℂ (solutionSpace p) = Module.finrank ℂ (residualSpace L) := by
  rw [finrank_solutionSpace hp, finrank_residualSpace, hdeg]

/-! ## Kernel transfer and the determinant criterion -/

/-- A square matrix has vanishing determinant exactly when its kernel is nontrivial. -/
theorem det_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot {n : ℕ} (N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) :
    N.det = 0 ↔ LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin N) ≠ ⊥ := by
  constructor
  · intro hdet
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hNv⟩ := Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff.mpr hdet
    intro hbot
    have hmem : v ∈ LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin N) := by
      simpa [LinearMap.mem_ker] using hNv
    rw [hbot, Submodule.mem_bot] at hmem
    exact hv hmem
  · intro hne
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hvne⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hne
    refine Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff.mp ⟨v, hvne, ?_⟩
    simpa [LinearMap.mem_ker] using hv

/-- **Equations (8)–(9).**  Under the kernel isomorphism, the eigenspace is trivial exactly when the
square Evans determinant is nonzero. -/
theorem eigenspace_eq_bot_iff_det_ne_zero {n : ℕ} {N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ}
    {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] {K : Submodule ℂ V}
    (e : K ≃ₗ[ℂ] LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin N)) :
    K = ⊥ ↔ N.det ≠ 0 := by
  have key : K ≠ ⊥ ↔ LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin N) ≠ ⊥ := by
    constructor
    · intro hK hkbot
      obtain ⟨u, hu, hune⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hK
      have h1 : ((e ⟨u, hu⟩ : LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin N)) : Fin n → ℂ) = 0 := by
        have hmem := (e ⟨u, hu⟩).2
        exact (Submodule.eq_bot_iff _).mp hkbot _ hmem
      have h2 : e ⟨u, hu⟩ = 0 := Subtype.ext h1
      have h3 : (⟨u, hu⟩ : K) = 0 := by
        have h4 := congrArg e.symm h2
        rwa [LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply, map_zero] at h4
      exact hune (congrArg Subtype.val h3)
    · intro hk hKbot
      obtain ⟨v, hv, hvne⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hk
      have h1 : ((e.symm ⟨v, hv⟩ : K) : V) = 0 := by
        have hmem := (e.symm ⟨v, hv⟩).2
        exact (Submodule.eq_bot_iff _).mp hKbot _ hmem
      have h2 : e.symm ⟨v, hv⟩ = 0 := Subtype.ext h1
      have h3 : (⟨v, hv⟩ : LinearMap.ker (Matrix.mulVecLin N)) = 0 := by
        have h4 := congrArg e h2
        rwa [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, map_zero] at h4
      exact hvne (congrArg Subtype.val h3)
  constructor
  · intro hK hdet
    exact (key.mpr ((det_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot N).mp hdet)) hK
  · intro hdet
    by_contra hK
    exact hdet ((det_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot N).mpr (key.mp hK))

/-!
# Eventual positive trace of the literal CCM pole matrix

The actual CCM pole diagonal has the same one-sided Gamma boundary primitive as the
exponential-pole diagonal whose sharp asymptotic is already formalized.  This transfers its
positive genus limit to the literal CCM matrix.  Consequently the large-aperture two-pole
compression cannot have two negative parity energies: once its determinant wall is crossed,
exactly one parity is negative.

This is a trace law only.  It neither controls the off-diagonal entry nor proves the
RH-equivalent determinant inequality.
-/

open Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The actual CCM and exponential-pole self-boundary primitives are definitionally the same
one-sided Gamma integral. -/
theorem ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryPrimitive_eq_poleSelfBoundaryPrimitive (s : ℝ) :
    ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryPrimitive s = poleSelfBoundaryPrimitive s := by
  rfl

/-- The literal CCM pole diagonal is the sharp exponential-pole diagonal at the same aperture. -/
theorem ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_eq_poleDiagonalExplicit (a : SuzukiPositiveAperture) :
    ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a = poleDiagonalExplicit a.1 := by
  rw [ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_eq_error,
    ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryMass_eq_primitive,
    ccmGammaPoleSelfBoundaryPrimitive_eq_poleSelfBoundaryPrimitive]
  rfl

/-- **Eventual positive trace.**  The trace coordinate of the literal CCM two-pole matrix is
strictly positive beyond one unconditional aperture threshold. -/
theorem exists_eventually_ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_pos :
    ∃ A : ℝ, ∀ a : SuzukiPositiveAperture, A ≤ a.1 →
      0 < ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a := by
  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := eventually_atTop.1 eventually_poleDiagonalExplicit_pos
  refine ⟨A, fun a ha => ?_⟩
  rw [ccmWeilPoleDiagonal_eq_poleDiagonalExplicit]
  exact hA a.1 ha

/-- Above the positive-trace threshold, a strict pole-compression wall crossing has one and only
one negative parity energy.  The other parity remains strictly positive. -/
theorem ccmWeilPoleCompression_parity_opposite_sign_of_diagonal_pos_of_cross_exceeds
    (a : SuzukiPositiveAperture)
    (hdiag : 0 < ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a)
    (hcross : ccmWeilPoleDiagonal a < |ccmWeilPoleCross a|) :
    (ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a 1) < 0 ∧
      0 < ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a (-1))) ∨
    (0 < ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a 1) ∧
      ccmRestrictedWeilSourceQuadratic a (ccmPolarParityFormVector a (-1)) < 0) := by
  rw [ccmWeilPoleCompression_parity_energy a (Or.inl rfl),
    ccmWeilPoleCompression_parity_energy a (Or.inr rfl)]
  rcases le_total 0 (ccmWeilPoleCross a) with hnonneg | hnonpos
  · right
    rw [abs_of_nonneg hnonneg] at hcross
    constructor <;> nlinarith
  · left
    rw [abs_of_nonpos hnonpos] at hcross
    constructor <;> nlinarith

end

# Weil cone and PBAP in the Lean corpus

Status on 7 October 2026. This report distinguishes unconditional theorems, implications with open hypotheses, excluded constructions, and problems still open in the searched corpus.

**The corpus proves the existence reformulation and many strong rigidity theorems. It does not supply an unconditional integer-supported Weil-positive system, an unconditional proof of PBAP, or a general implication from mere existence to RH.** The remaining gap is mathematical, not just an unformalized compactness or spectral-representation argument.

## Exact objects and logical status

Write \(\Lambda\) for the von Mangoldt function and \(\lambda:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\). Values at 0 and 1 are irrelevant to the Weil functional; equality statements generally concern \(n\ge2\).

Two different positivity predicates occur:

- `RHTower.WeilPositive`: positivity at every aperture on compactly supported \(C^2\) tests whose Fourier transforms vanish at both polar points \(\pm i/2\).
- `RHTower.WeilPositiveFull`: positivity on **all** compactly supported \(C^2\) autocorrelation tests, retaining the pole term.

Neither definition requires \(\lambda(n)\ge0\). “Weil-positive” describes the quadratic form, not the signs of its coefficients. The full predicate implies the polar predicate. This audit did not locate a converse for arbitrary weights; the two versions must not be interchanged.

For the full cone, set \(\mathcal W=\{\lambda:\operatorname{WeilPositiveFull}(\lambda)\}\). In the corpus's normalization,

\[
Q_\lambda(f)=A_{\rm full}(f)-\sum_{n\ge2}\lambda(n)L_n(f),
\]

where \(A_{\rm full}\) contains the archimedean **and pole** contributions and \(L_n\) is the real symmetric autocorrelation value at \(\pm\log n\), divided by \(\sqrt n\). Each individual compactly supported test sees finitely many integers.

Full PBAP says: every finite nonnegative combination of tests with \(\sum_i\alpha_iL_n(f_i)=0\) for **every integer** \(n\ge2\) has nonnegative combined \(A_{\rm full}\). It is not blindness only at primes, and the underlying test functions need not be nonnegative.

## What has been proved beyond the reformulation

### Compactness and the finite to infinite passage

For polar positivity, existence at every finite aperture implies existence of one system positive at all apertures. The weights may depend on the aperture before taking the compactness limit. [Finite-level existence theorem](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilPositivityFiniteLevelExistence.lean:119).

For full positivity, the normalized cone \(\lambda(0)=\lambda(1)=0\) is compact in the product topology. More sharply,

\[
\mathrm{RH}\iff\forall N\;\exists\lambda\in\mathcal W\quad
\lambda(n)=\Lambda(n)\quad(2\le n\le N).
\]

The extension must already satisfy **all** full-cone tests. Checking a finite matrix of test vectors is weaker. Compactness supplies the passage to a limit; producing the compatible positive extensions remains open. [Compactness](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilFullConeCompactness.lean:166), [finite-prefix criterion](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilFullConeCompactness.lean:177).

### An exact extremal target

An explicit Riemann-kernel functional \(\ell\) satisfies

\[
\lambda\in\mathcal W\Longrightarrow
\ell(\lambda-\Lambda)\le0,
\qquad
\ell(\lambda-\Lambda)=0\Longrightarrow\lambda=\Lambda.
\]

# An explicit Weil-positive system for ζ's archimedean datum: Lebesgue measure minus one atom

- **ID:** weil-explicit-real-producer
- **Stage:** 3-formalized (paper proof and Lean, 2026-10-05)
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) + THEOREM (Lean, full Weil-positivity statement)
- **Source:** `1-in-progress/hf-positive-hodge-attack/krein-producer-loops.md`, L131
- **Statement:** `lam₀ = 1_{(1,∞)}dx − e^{1/20000}δ_{e^{1/10000}}` is Weil-positive for ζ's archimedean datum (pole weight 1). Its Weil measure is absolutely continuous with density `2[θ'(t) + Re(1/(½+it)) + cos(t/10⁴)] ≥ 1/100`, so the form is coercive.

## Goal
- **Existence over ℝ.** The Weil cone of ζ's archimedean datum, relaxed to signed measures on `(1,∞)`, has nonempty interior. Positivity is produced by the pole density (Lebesgue) plus one negative correction near `x = 1`, which pays for the low-frequency deficit `½ψ(5/4) − ½log π = −0.686` of Γ_ℝ.
- **Localization of RH.** For integer-supported systems, existence (W ≠ ∅, PBAP) is open and RH-strength. The present theorem shows that the whole difficulty is integrality of the support (plus sign), not the archimedean datum.

## Proof (paper)
1. In log coordinates, `T_{lam₀} = arch + e^{−|u|/2} + δ_{u₀} + δ_{−u₀}` with `u₀ = 10^{−4}`. The Lebesgue part cancels `e^{|u|/2}` from the pole term exactly, and the atom enters with weight `e^{u₀/2}e^{−u₀/2} = 1`.
2. `FT(T) = 2θ' + 1/(¼+t²) + 2cos(u₀t) = 2[½Re ψ(5/4+it/2) − ½log π + cos(u₀t)]`, using `½ψ(s/2) + 1/s = ½ψ(s/2+1)`.
3. The bracket is `≥ 1/200` for all `t` (Lean).
4. `T` is tempered with `FT(T) ≥ 0`, so it is positive definite (Bochner–Schwartz). ∎

# Full square-summable Xi--Weil positivity criterion

- **ID:** `xi-weil-full-square-summable-positivity-criterion`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM / FORMALIZATION / BRIDGE / NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE
- **Lean module:**

## Statement

Let `xiWeilPolarization` be the multiplicity-exact Hermitian polarization on the centered Xi
divisor. Lean proves

\[
\mathrm{RH}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Re\langle F,F\rangle_{\Xi,\mathrm{Weil}}\ge0
\quad\text{for every square-summable divisor test }F.
\]

The reverse implication is constructive. For a nonreal centered divisor point `alpha`, define

\[
F_\alpha(z)=
\begin{cases}
1,&z=\alpha,\\
-1,&z=\overline\alpha,\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

This test has finite divisor support and is therefore square-summable. Its exact Weil square is

\[
\langle F_\alpha,F_\alpha\rangle_{\Xi,\mathrm{Weil}}
=-#\{q:\lambda_q\in\{\alpha,\overline\alpha\}\}<0.
\]

Thus every nonreal divisor orbit produces an explicit negative square, including multiple zeros;
no derivative or simplicity assumption is required.

## Positive carrier law

Every successful Connes--Consani--Moscovici or Weil implementation must extend its source-side
positive form to a carrier containing these finite conjugate-orbit sign tests. The normalized
Cauchy-pole exhaustion theorem now proves that regular moving two-pole packets already approach
every such sign test. A test space which is not closed under that cofinal pole approach has not yet
carried the RH-deciding incidence.

The existing formal corpus already supplies:

- the Hermitian Xi-divisor polarization;
- the exact prime-plus-archimedean relative-resolvent formula on separated finite Cauchy packets;
- the algebraic and closed Hilbert Cauchy cores.

The remaining CCM theorem is therefore smaller than full Cauchy-core density: the distinguished
semilocal source form must be shown positive on every regular two-pole Cauchy packet while retaining
the normalized cofinal pole limit. Lean proves that this rank-two positivity already forces RH.

/-!
# Removing primes destroys Weil positivity

For a set `R` of primes, let `Λ_R(n) = Λ(n)` unless `n` is a power of a prime in `R`, and
`Λ_R(n) = 0` otherwise: the von Mangoldt function of `ζ(s) ∏_{p ∈ R}(1 - p^{-s})`.  Removing finitely
many Euler factors does not move the zeros of `ζ` in the critical strip (the new zeros lie on
`Re s = 0`), but it destroys Weil positivity for the archimedean datum of `ζ`, unconditionally:
`Λ_R ≤ Λ`, and a full-cone Weil-positive minorant of `Λ` equals `Λ`
(`eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_le`).
-/

namespace RHTower
namespace RemovedPrimes

open ArithmeticFunction

/-- The von Mangoldt function with the powers of the primes in `R` removed. -/
noncomputable def vonMangoldtWithout (R : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Set.indicator {m | ¬ ∃ p ∈ R, ∃ k, m = p ^ k} (fun m => (vonMangoldt m : ℝ)) n

theorem vonMangoldtWithout_le (R : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    vonMangoldtWithout R n ≤ (vonMangoldt n : ℝ) :=
  Set.indicator_le_self' (fun _ _ => vonMangoldt_nonneg) n

/-- **Removing any prime destroys Weil positivity.**  If `R` contains a prime, then the von Mangoldt
function with the powers of the primes of `R` removed is not full-cone Weil-positive. -/
theorem not_weilPositiveFull_vonMangoldtWithout {R : Set ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpR : p ∈ R) :
    ¬ WeilPositiveFull (vonMangoldtWithout R) := by
  intro hW
  have h := eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_le hW fun n _ => vonMangoldtWithout_le R n
  have hp2 := h p hp.two_le
  have hmem : p ∉ {m : ℕ | ¬ ∃ q ∈ R, ∃ k, m = q ^ k} := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, not_not]
    exact ⟨p, hpR, 1, (pow_one p).symm⟩
  have h0 : vonMangoldtWithout R p = 0 := Set.indicator_of_notMem hmem _
  rw [h0, vonMangoldt_apply_prime hp] at hp2
  exact (Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast hp.one_lt)).ne' hp2.symm

/-- In particular, the von Mangoldt function of `(1 - 2^{-s}) ζ(s)` (the prime `2` removed) is not
full-cone Weil-positive. -/
theorem not_weilPositiveFull_without_two :
    ¬ WeilPositiveFull (vonMangoldtWithout {2}) :=
  not_weilPositiveFull_vonMangoldtWithout Nat.prime_two rfl

/-- **Full-cone form.** -/
theorem eq_zero_of_weilPositiveFull_add (hR : RegularDeviation w E)

/-- The quadratic form only sees the support of `c`. -/
theorem lagGramForm_subset {S T : Finset ℝ} (hTS : T ⊆ S) {c : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ x ∈ S, x ∉ T → c x = 0) : lagGramForm S c = lagGramForm T c := by
  unfold lagGramForm
  rw [← Finset.sum_subset hTS (fun x hx hx' => by rw [hc x hx hx']; simp)]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
  rw [← Finset.sum_subset hTS (fun y hy hy' => by rw [hc y hy hy']; simp)]

/-- The `2×2` minor on `{1, n}` with weights `1, −1` is `2(a_1 − a_n)`. -/
theorem lagGramForm_pair {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {c : ℝ → ℝ} (hc1 : c 1 = 1) (hcn : c n = -1) :
    lagGramForm {(1 : ℝ), (n : ℝ)} c = 2 * (poleSharpConstant - integerLag n) := by
  classical
  have hne : (1 : ℝ) ≠ (n : ℝ) := by
    have : (2 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
    linarith
  unfold lagGramForm
  rw [Finset.sum_pair hne, Finset.sum_pair hne, Finset.sum_pair hne, hc1, hcn]
  rw [lagGramKernel_self, lagGramKernel_self, lagGramKernel_symm (n : ℝ) 1]
  unfold lagGramKernel integerLag
  rw [Real.log_one, zero_sub, weilLagFunctionReal_neg]
  ring

/-- **RH ⟺ the lag kernel is positive semidefinite on the positive reals.** -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_iff_lagGramKernel_posSemidef :
    RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∀ (S : Finset ℝ) (c : ℝ → ℝ), 0 ≤ lagGramForm S c := by
  classical
  refine ⟨fun h S c => lagGramForm_nonneg_of_riemannHypothesis h S c, fun h => ?_⟩
  rw [riemannHypothesis_iff_integerLag_le_sharp]
  intro n hn
  have := h {(1 : ℝ), (n : ℝ)} (fun x => if x = 1 then 1 else -1)
  have hne : (1 : ℝ) ≠ (n : ℝ) := by
    have : (2 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
    linarith
  rw [lagGramForm_pair hn (by simp) (by simp [hne.symm])] at this
  linarith

/-- The arithmetic Gram form: the kernel on the integers `1, …, N`, i.e. on the divisor group
of `Spec ℤ` generated by the primes up to `N`. -/
def arithmeticGramForm (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, c n * c m * lagGramKernel n m

theorem arithmeticGramForm_eq (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) :
    arithmeticGramForm N c
      = lagGramForm ((Finset.Icc 1 N).image (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))) (fun x => c ⌊x⌋₊) := by
  classical
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) (Finset.Icc 1 N : Set ℕ) := fun a _ b _ hab =>
    Nat.cast_injective hab
  unfold arithmeticGramForm lagGramForm
  rw [Finset.sum_image hinj]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun n _ => ?_
  rw [Finset.sum_image hinj]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun m _ => ?_
  simp [Nat.floor_natCast]

/-- **RH ⟺ every arithmetic Gram matrix `(Φ(log(n/m)))_{n,m ≤ N}` is positive semidefinite.** -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_iff_arithmeticGramForm_nonneg :
    RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∀ (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ), 0 ≤ arithmeticGramForm N c := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro h N c
    rw [arithmeticGramForm_eq]
    exact lagGramForm_nonneg_of_riemannHypothesis h _ _
  · intro h
    rw [riemannHypothesis_iff_integerLag_le_sharp]
    intro n hn
    have hne : (1 : ℝ) ≠ (n : ℝ) := by
      have : (2 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
      linarith
    set c₀ : ℕ → ℝ := fun k => if k = 1 then 1 else if k = n then -1 else 0 with hc₀
    have hpair := h n c₀
    rw [arithmeticGramForm_eq] at hpair
    have hsub : ({(1 : ℝ), (n : ℝ)} : Finset ℝ) ⊆ (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (fun k : ℕ => (k : ℝ)) := by
      intro x hx
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx
      rcases hx with rfl | rfl
      · exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨1, by rw [Finset.mem_Icc]; omega, by simp⟩
      · exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨n, by rw [Finset.mem_Icc]; omega, rfl⟩
    have hvan : ∀ x ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (fun k : ℕ => (k : ℝ)),
        x ∉ ({(1 : ℝ), (n : ℝ)} : Finset ℝ) → (fun x => c₀ ⌊x⌋₊) x = 0 := by
      intro x hx hx'
      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hx
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, not_or] at hx'
      have hk1 : k ≠ 1 := fun h => hx'.1 (by rw [h]; simp)
      have hkn : k ≠ n := fun h => hx'.2 (by rw [h])
      simp [hc₀, Nat.floor_natCast, hk1, hkn]
    rw [lagGramForm_subset hsub hvan] at hpair
    rw [lagGramForm_pair hn (by simp [hc₀]) (by
      simp only [hc₀, Nat.floor_natCast]
      have : n ≠ 1 := by omega
      simp [this])] at hpair
    linarith

end

/-!
# Weil-cone rigidity on finite unions of common-ratio geometric progressions

**Theorem** (`eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_commonRatio`).  Let `b ≥ 2` and let `C` be a
finite set of natural numbers.  If `lam` is full-cone Weil-positive for the archimedean datum of `ζ`
and `lam(n) = Λ(n)` for every `n ≥ 2` outside `S = ⋃_{c ∈ C} {c b^j : j ≥ 0}`, then `lam = Λ`.

The cosets may be arbitrarily close (e.g. `{1000·2^j} ∪ {1001·2^j}`, logarithmic gap `≈ 10⁻³`,
`eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_thousand`), and the deviation on `S` is arbitrary.

**Proof.** `S` is a finite union of geometric progressions, so `Σ_{n ∈ S} n^{−1/4}` is a finite sum
of geometric series (`summable_commonRatioSet_rpow`), and the abscissa rigidity of the Weil cone for
sparse supports (`WeilAbscissa.eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_sparse_rpow`, exponent `τ < 1/2`)
applies.
-/

open Classical

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower.WeilCommonRatio

/-- `n` lies in one of the cosets `c·b^ℕ`, `c ∈ C`. -/
def commonRatioSet (b : ℕ) (C : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ c ∈ C, ∃ j : ℕ, n = c * b ^ j

/-- The weight `n^{−1/4}` on the single coset `c·b^ℕ`. -/
def cosetWeight (b c n : ℕ) : ℝ := if ∃ j : ℕ, n = c * b ^ j then (n : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)) else 0

theorem cosetWeight_nonneg (b c n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ cosetWeight b c n := by
  unfold cosetWeight
  split_ifs
  · exact Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg n) _
  · exact le_rfl

/-- A single coset carries a convergent geometric series. -/
theorem summable_cosetWeight {b : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (c : ℕ) : Summable (cosetWeight b c) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with rfl | hc
  · have h0 : cosetWeight b 0 = fun _ => 0 := by
      funext n
      unfold cosetWeight
      split_ifs with h
      · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := h
        simp
      · rfl
    rw [h0]
    exact summable_zero
  · set g : ℕ → ℕ := fun j => c * b ^ j with hg
    have hb1 : 1 < b := by omega
    have hginj : Function.Injective g := by
      intro i j hij
      simp only [hg] at hij
      exact Nat.pow_right_injective hb (Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left hc hij)
    have hzero : ∀ n ∉ Set.range g, cosetWeight b c n = 0 := by
      intro n hn
      unfold cosetWeight
      rw [if_neg]
      rintro ⟨j, rfl⟩
      exact hn ⟨j, rfl⟩
    refine (hginj.summable_iff hzero).mp ?_
    have hr0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (b : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)) := Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg b) _
    have hr1 : (b : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)) < 1 :=
      Real.rpow_lt_one_of_one_lt_of_neg (by exact_mod_cast hb1) (by norm_num)
    refine ((summable_geometric_of_lt_one hr0 hr1).mul_left ((c : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)))).congr
      fun j => ?_
    simp only [Function.comp, hg, cosetWeight]
    rw [if_pos ⟨j, rfl⟩]
    push_cast
    rw [Real.mul_rpow (Nat.cast_nonneg c) (pow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg b) j),
      ← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_mul (Nat.cast_nonneg b),
      ← Real.rpow_mul (Nat.cast_nonneg b), mul_comm (j : ℝ)]

/-- **Summability on a finite union of common-ratio progressions.** -/
theorem summable_commonRatioSet_rpow {b : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (C : Finset ℕ) :
    Summable fun n : ℕ => if commonRatioSet b C n then (n : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)) else 0 := by
  refine Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => ?_) (fun n => ?_)
    (summable_sum (s := C) fun c _ => summable_cosetWeight hb c)
  · split_ifs
    · exact Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg n) _
    · exact le_rfl
  · split_ifs with h
    · obtain ⟨c, hc, hj⟩ := h
      have hval : cosetWeight b c n = (n : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)) := by
        unfold cosetWeight; rw [if_pos hj]
      rw [← hval]
      exact Finset.single_le_sum (fun c' _ => cosetWeight_nonneg b c' n) hc
    · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun c' _ => cosetWeight_nonneg b c' n

/-- **Weil-cone rigidity on every finite union of common-ratio geometric progressions.**  A full-cone
Weil-positive `lam` that agrees with `Λ` off `⋃_{c ∈ C} c·b^ℕ` (`b ≥ 2`) equals `Λ`. -/
theorem eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_commonRatio {lam : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hW : RHTower.WeilPositiveFull lam) {b : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (C : Finset ℕ)
    (hoff : ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → ¬ commonRatioSet b C n → lam n = ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n) :
    ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → lam n = ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n :=
  RHTower.WeilAbscissa.eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_sparse_rpow hW (τ := 1 / 4)
    (by norm_num) (summable_commonRatioSet_rpow hb C) hoff

/-- **Instance at logarithmic gap `log(1001/1000)`.**  A full-cone Weil-positive `lam` with
`lam(n) = Λ(n)` off `{1000·2^j} ∪ {1001·2^j}` equals `Λ`. -/
theorem eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_thousand {lam : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hW : RHTower.WeilPositiveFull lam)
    (hoff : ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → (¬ ∃ j : ℕ, n = 1000 * 2 ^ j) → (¬ ∃ j : ℕ, n = 1001 * 2 ^ j) →
      lam n = ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n) :
    ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → lam n = ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n := by
  refine eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_commonRatio hW (b := 2) le_rfl {1000, 1001}

/-!
# Weil-cone rigidity on finitely generated multiplicative supports

**Theorem** (`eq_zero_of_positiveDefinite_neg_nullPotential`). Let `P` be a finite set of primes
and `v : ℕ → ℝ` supported on the `P`-smooth numbers `n ≥ 2`, with `|v(n)| ≤ 2 log n + A`. If the
null potential `−ψ_v`, `ψ_v(y) = Σ_n v(n)(K(y + log n) + K(y − log n))`, is positive definite, then
`v = 0`.

**Proof.** Fix `n₀` with `v(n₀) ≠ 0` and the sign `ε` of `v(n₀)`. Pair Bochner's measure of `−ψ_v`
with the `|ζ|²` notch test of weight `q(t) = |1 + ε n₀^{it}|² Π_{p∈P} |1 − p^{−1/2+it}|²`
(`sum_mul_re_weightedMoment_nonpos`): `Σ_n v(n) Re M_q(log n) ≤ 0`. At a smooth twist the Euler
factors cancel the lifted diagonal except at `n = n₀` (`exists_norm_weightedMoment_sub_main_le`), so
`|v(n₀)| Π_p(1 − 1/p) ∫ ω log t` is bounded by the diagonal remainders `O(L)`, the near-resonant and
Gaussian terms of the twists with `log n ≤ M`, and the crude tail of the twists with `log n > M`.
With `L = M^{8J}` every error is `O(L)` while `∫ ω log t ≥ L log L`; letting `M → ∞` forces
`v(n₀) = 0`.
-/

noncomputable section

/-! ## Exponent vectors of smooth twists -/

theorem vecNum_mul_vecDen_eq (b : P → ℤ) :
    vecNum b * vecDen b = ∏ p : P, (p : ℕ) ^ (b p).natAbs := by
  unfold vecNum vecDen
  rw [← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun p _ => ?_
  rw [← pow_add, Int.toNat_add_toNat_neg_eq_natAbs]

theorem prod_pow_factorization_eq {n : ℕ} (hn : IsSmoothOver P n) :
    ∏ p : P, (p : ℕ) ^ n.factorization p = n := by
  have hn0 : n ≠ 0 := by have := hn.1; omega
  rw [Finset.prod_coe_sort P (fun p => p ^ n.factorization p),
    ← Finsupp.prod_of_support_subset _ (by rw [Nat.support_factorization]; exact hn.2)
      (fun p k => p ^ k) (fun p _ => pow_zero p)]
  exact Nat.prod_factorization_pow_eq_self hn0

theorem vecNum_vecOf {n : ℕ} (hn : IsSmoothOver P n) : vecNum (vecOf P n) = n := by
  unfold vecNum vecOf
  simp only [Int.toNat_natCast]
  exact prod_pow_factorization_eq hn

theorem vecDen_vecOf (n : ℕ) : vecDen (vecOf P n) = 1 := by
  unfold vecDen vecOf
  refine Finset.prod_eq_one fun p _ => ?_
  have : (-(n.factorization p : ℤ)).toNat = 0 := by omega
  rw [this, pow_zero]

theorem inv_sqrt_eq_prod_primeHalf {n : ℕ} (hn : IsSmoothOver P n) :
    (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ = ∏ p : P, primeHalf p ^ n.factorization p := by
  have h := inv_sqrt_vecNum_mul_vecDen (vecOf P n)
  rw [vecNum_vecOf hn, vecDen_vecOf, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at h
  rw [h]
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun p _ => ?_
  simp [vecOf]

/-- The twist bound `K₀ = Π_p p^{v_p(n₀) + 1}`. -/
def twistBound (P : Finset ℕ) (n₀ : ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ p : P, (p : ℕ) ^ (n₀.factorization p + 1)

theorem twistBound_pos (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) (n₀ : ℕ) : 0 < twistBound P n₀ :=
  Finset.prod_pos fun p _ => pow_pos (hP p p.2).pos _

/-- The coordinates of a mode twist `b = v(n) − (j v(n₀) + c)`. -/
theorem mode_coord_bounds {n n₀ : ℕ} {j : ℤ} (hj : j ∈ bohrModes) {c : P → ℤ}
    (hc : c ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : P => bohrModes)) (p : P) :
    (n.factorization p : ℤ) ≤ ((vecOf P n - (j • vecOf P n₀ + c)) p).natAbs +
        (n₀.factorization p + 1 : ℕ) ∧
      (((vecOf P n - (j • vecOf P n₀ + c)) p).natAbs : ℤ) ≤
        n.factorization p + (n₀.factorization p + 1 : ℕ) ∧
      ((-(vecOf P n - (j • vecOf P n₀ + c)) p).toNat : ℤ) ≤ (n₀.factorization p + 1 : ℕ) := by
  have hcp : c p ∈ bohrModes := Fintype.mem_piFinset.mp hc p
  unfold bohrModes at hj hcp
  simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hj hcp
  simp only [vecOf, Pi.sub_apply, Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
  rcases hj with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hcp with h | h | h <;> rw [h] <;> omega

theorem sqrt_twistBound_eq (P : Finset ℕ) (n₀ : ℕ) :
    Real.sqrt (twistBound P n₀) = ∏ p : P, Real.sqrt (p : ℕ) ^ (n₀.factorization p + 1) := by
  have hsq : ((twistBound P n₀ : ℕ) : ℝ) =
      (∏ p : P, Real.sqrt (p : ℕ) ^ (n₀.factorization p + 1)) ^ 2 := by
    unfold twistBound
    push_cast
    rw [← Finset.prod_pow]
    refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun p _ => ?_
    rw [← pow_mul, mul_comm, pow_mul, Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg _)]
  rw [hsq, Real.sqrt_sq (Finset.prod_nonneg fun p _ => by positivity)]

/-- The weight of a mode twist is at most `√K₀ · n_P^{−1/2}`, `n_P = Π_{p∈P} p^{v_p(n)}`. -/
theorem weight_mode_le_prod (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) {n n₀ : ℕ} {j : ℤ} (hj : j ∈ bohrModes)
    {c : P → ℤ} (hc : c ∈ Fintype.piFinset (fun _ : P => bohrModes)) :
    ∏ p : P, primeHalf p ^ ((vecOf P n - (j • vecOf P n₀ + c)) p).natAbs ≤
      Real.sqrt (twistBound P n₀) *
        (Real.sqrt ((∏ p : P, (p : ℕ) ^ n.factorization p : ℕ) : ℝ))⁻¹ := by
  have hinv : (Real.sqrt ((∏ p : P, (p : ℕ) ^ n.factorization p : ℕ) : ℝ))⁻¹ =
      ∏ p : P, primeHalf p ^ n.factorization p := by

_mul_of_nonneg_left (hEb n hn) (abs_nonneg _)
        _ = _ := by ring
    have h2 : ∑ n ∈ F, |v n| * (1 + Real.log n) * (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ ≤ rankinConst J * S :=
      (hsR.sum_le_tsum F fun n _ => by have := one_add_log_nonneg n; positivity).trans hR
    have h3 : ∑ n ∈ F, |v n| ≤ (1 + M) ^ J * S :=
      sum_abs_le_of_log_le hs hM0 fun n hn => ((hFmem n).mp hn).2
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum] at h1
    refine h1.trans ?_

        ≤ B * (2 * L * Real.sqrt K₀ * C₅) * (rankinConst J * S) +
            B * C_T * U * ((1 + M) ^ J * S) := by
          gcongr
      _ = B * (2 * Real.sqrt K₀ * C₅ * (rankinConst J * S)) * L +

      _ ≤ B * (2 * Real.sqrt K₀ * C₅ * (rankinConst J * S)) * L +

            ≤ |v n| * (C_M * L ^ 3 * ((1 + Real.log n) ^ (25 * J))⁻¹) :=
              mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ((Complex.abs_re_le_norm _).trans (hMdec n))
                (abs_nonneg _)
          _ = _ := by ring
  have hhs : Summable (fun n => if n ∈ F then 0 else f n) :=
    Summable.of_norm_bounded (htail.1.mul_left (C_M * L ^ 3)) hhle
  have htailb : |∑' n, (if n ∈ F then 0 else f n)| ≤ C_M * S * L := by

          refine (norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm hhs.norm).trans (le_of_eq ?_)

      _ ≤ ∑' n : ℕ, C_M * L ^ 3 *
            (if Real.log n ≤ M then 0 else |v n| * ((1 + Real.log n) ^ (25 * J))⁻¹) :=
          hhs.abs.tsum_le_tsum hhle (htail.1.mul_left _)
      _ = C_M * L ^ 3 * ∑' n : ℕ,
            (if Real.log n ≤ M then 0 else |v n| * ((1 + Real.log n) ^ (25 * J))⁻¹) :=

          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left htail.2 (by positivity)

          rw [show 25 * J - J = 24 * J by omega]

/-! ## The theorem -/

/-- **Weil-cone rigidity on finitely generated multiplicative supports.** If `v` is supported on
the `P`-smooth numbers, `|v(n)| ≤ 2 log n + A`, and `−ψ_v` is positive definite, then `v = 0`. -/
theorem eq_zero_of_positiveDefinite_neg_nullPotential (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) {v : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hsupp : ∀ n, v n ≠ 0 → IsSmoothOver P n) {A : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A)
    (ha : ∀ n, |v n| ≤ 2 * Real.log n + A)
    (hPD : PositiveDefiniteOnReal fun y => ((-RHTower.WeilRegular.nullPotential v y : ℝ) : ℂ)) :
    v = 0 := by
  funext n₀
  by_contra hne
  have hn₀ := hsupp n₀ hne
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := exists_key_bound hP hsupp hA ha hPD hn₀
  set J : ℕ := 2 * P.card + 2 with hJ
  have hJ0 : (0 : ℝ) < 8 * J := by positivity
  set a : ℝ := |v n₀| * ∏ p : P, (1 - primeHalf p ^ 2) with ha'
  have ha0 : 0 < a := mul_pos (abs_pos.mpr hne) (eulerProduct_pos hP)
  -- choose `M` with `a · 8J log M > C`
  set M : ℝ := max (max 2 (Real.log n₀)) (Real.exp (|C| / (a * (8 * J)) + 1)) with hM
  have hM2 : 2 ≤ M := (le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_left _ _)
  have hMn : Real.log n₀ ≤ M := (le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_left _ _)
  have hMe : Real.exp (|C| / (a * (8 * J)) + 1) ≤ M := le_max_right _ _
  have hM0 : 0 < M := by linarith

/-!
# Suzuki's restricted Weil form with every source parameter discharged

`SuzukiRestrictedWeilForm` assembled the four distributional blocks but deliberately left the
smooth remainder and finite prime aperture as parameters.  This file inserts Suzuki's literal
source data:

* `A = (log(2π) - ψ(2))/2`;
* visible indices `2 ≤ n ≤ exp(2a)`;
* the continuous even remainder kernel proved in
  `SuzukiWeilRemainderRegularity`.

The resulting form and representative contain no free analytic kernel.  We also prove the exact
atomic Dirichlet decomposition and unconditional lower bound for its complete visible-prime
sector.  The only remaining semiboundedness work is therefore the finite-part block; smooth
remainder boundedness is now a theorem of the literal source.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set

noncomputable section

/-- Literal real smooth core of Suzuki's restricted form.  Regularity and aperture support are
intrinsic data, so source theorems need no external analytic premises. -/
structure SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore (a : ℝ) where
  toFun : ℝ → ℝ
  smooth : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) toFun
  supportRadius : ℝ
  supportRadius_nonneg : 0 ≤ supportRadius
  supportRadius_lt_aperture : supportRadius < a
  support_subset : Function.support toFun ⊆ Icc (-supportRadius) supportRadius

instance (a : ℝ) : CoeFun (SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) fun _ => ℝ → ℝ :=
  ⟨SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.toFun⟩

theorem SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.continuous {a : ℝ}
    (u : SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) : Continuous u :=
  u.smooth.continuous

theorem SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.hasCompactSupport {a : ℝ}
    (u : SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) : HasCompactSupport u :=
  HasCompactSupport.of_support_subset_isCompact isCompact_Icc u.support_subset

theorem SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore.support_subset_aperture {a : ℝ}
    (u : SuzukiRestrictedWeilCore a) : Function.support u ⊆ Ioo (-a) a := by
  intro x hx
  have hxr := u.support_subset hx
  constructor
  · linarith [hxr.1, u.supportRadius_lt_aperture]
  · linarith [hxr.2, u.supportRadius_lt_aperture]

/-- Suzuki's exact scalar coefficient in the local screw expansion. -/
def suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant : ℝ :=
  (Real.log (2 * Real.pi) - (Complex.digamma (2 : ℂ)).re) / 2

/-- Prime powers visible in the difference interval `[-2a,2a]`. -/
def suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices (a : ℝ) : Finset ℕ :=
  RHTower.suzukiVisibleWeilIndices (2 * a)

/-- Literal source-locked restricted Weil form at aperture `a`. -/
def suzukiRestrictedWeilForm (a : ℝ) (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  restrictedWeilForm a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant
    (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u φ

/-- Literal source-locked distributional representative. -/
def suzukiRestrictedWeilRepresentative (a : ℝ) (u : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  restrictedWeilRepresentative a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant
    (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u

/-- The source-locked form is exactly Suzuki's four published blocks. -/
theorem suzukiRestrictedWeilForm_eq_fourBlocks (a : ℝ) (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) :
    suzukiRestrictedWeilForm a u φ =
      weilFinitePartBlock a u φ +
        weilScalarBlock a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant u φ +
        weilPrimeBlock (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) u φ +
        weilSmoothBlock a RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u φ := by
  rfl

/-- The source-locked four-block form uses exactly the curvature of Suzuki's origin remainder;
the independently derived hyperbolic and screw-kernel normalizations agree pointwise. -/
theorem suzukiRestrictedWeilForm_eq_originRemainderFourBlocks
    (a : ℝ) (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) :
    suzukiRestrictedWeilForm a u φ =
      weilFinitePartBlock a u φ +
        weilScalarBlock a suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant u φ +
        weilPrimeBlock (suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a) u φ +
        weilSmoothBlock a suzukiOriginRemainderCurvature u φ := by
  rw [suzukiRestrictedWeilForm_eq_fourBlocks]
  congr 1
  unfold weilSmoothBlock
  congr 1
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
  intro x _
  apply congrArg (fun z : ℝ => z * φ x)
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
  intro y _
  dsimp only
  rw [suzukiWeilRemainderKernel_eq_originCurvature]

/-- The source-locked representative has Suzuki's exact finite-part, scalar, prime, and smooth
convolution terms, with no kernel parameter left. -/
theorem suzukiRestrictedWeilRepresentative_eq (a : ℝ) (u : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) :
    suzukiRestrictedWeilRepresentative a u x =
      -(1 / 2) * cauchyFinitePart a x u -
        (2 * suzukiWeilArchimedeanConstant + 1) * u x -
        (∑ n ∈ suzukiRestrictedWeilIndices a,
          primePairWeight n * (u (x + Real.log n) + u (x - Real.log n))) +
        weilSmoothRepresentative a RHTower.suzukiWeilRemainderKernel u x := by
  rfl

theorem ccmGuinandWeilSineMomentMatrix_det_eq_zero_iff {N : ℕ}

/-- Finite packet with independent weights on an event and its source reflection, carried by the

    (forward reflected horizon : Fin N → ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin (N + 1)) (Fin (N + 1)) ℝ :=
  ∑ r, (forward r •
      ccmGuinandWeilEventMatrix
        (fun j : Fin (N + 1) => (j : ℤ)) (horizon r) +
    reflected r •
      ccmGuinandWeilEventMatrix
        (fun j : Fin (N + 1) => (j : ℤ)) (1 - horizon r))

/-!
# Forward coefficients of a full-positive arithmetic source

For every full-positive source, the forward Dirichlet-exponential coefficients
have critical square energy `sum (norm a(n))^2 / n = O(log N)`. The proof
retains the signed logarithmic convolution when inserting these coefficients
into the Weil--Toeplitz form, then uses a finite logarithmic-moment induction.

No multiplicativity or coefficient-order premise is required. This energy
bound does not assert uniform boundedness of the zeta quotient.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- Coefficients of the forward exponential, with the source truncated below two. -/
def forwardCoeff (lam : ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℂ :=
  dirichletExp (logZetaCoeff (fun n => if 2 ≤ n then lam n else 0))

@[simp] theorem forwardCoeff_zero (lam : ℕ → ℝ) : forwardCoeff lam 0 = 0 :=
  dirichletExp_zero

@[simp] theorem forwardCoeff_one (lam : ℕ → ℝ) : forwardCoeff lam 1 = 1 := by
  apply dirichletExp_one <;> simp [logZetaCoeff]

/-- Full positivity supplies the literal forward Dirichlet series on its
absolute half-plane, without coefficient ordering or multiplicativity. -/
theorem forwardCoeff_LSeries {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam)
    {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    LSeriesSummable (forwardCoeff lam) s ∧
      LSeries (forwardCoeff lam) s =
        cexp (LSeries (logZetaCoeff (fun n => if 2 ≤ n then lam n else 0)) s) := by
  have hH := WeilSpectral.herglotzWeilPositive_of_weilPositiveFull hW
  apply LSeries_dirichletExp (by simp [logZetaCoeff]) (by simp [logZetaCoeff])
  apply LSeriesSummable_of_abscissaOfAbsConv_lt_re
  exact (abscissaOfAbsConv_logZetaCoeff_le hH.summable).trans_lt (by exact_mod_cast hs)

private theorem forwardCoeff_abscissa_le {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) :
    LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv (forwardCoeff lam) ≤ 1 := by
  have h := LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_le_of_forall_lt_LSeriesSummable (x := 1)
    (fun y hy => (forwardCoeff_LSeries hW (s := y) (by simpa using hy)).1)
  exact_mod_cast h

/-- The exact logarithmic convolution of the forward coefficients. -/
theorem forwardCoeff_log_convolution {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (n : ℕ) :
    LSeries.convolution (WeilHerglotz.lamC lam) (forwardCoeff lam) n =
      (Real.log n : ℂ) * forwardCoeff lam n := by
  have hH := WeilSpectral.herglotzWeilPositive_of_weilPositiveFull hW
  have ha := forwardCoeff_abscissa_le hW
  have hlog : LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv (LSeries.logMul (forwardCoeff lam)) < ⊤ := by
    rw [LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv_logMul]
    exact ha.trans_lt (EReal.coe_lt_top 1)
  have hconv : LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv
      (LSeries.convolution (WeilHerglotz.lamC lam) (forwardCoeff lam)) < ⊤ := by
    have hLam : LSeriesSummable (WeilHerglotz.lamC lam) 2 :=
      WeilHerglotz.summable_term_lamC hW (by norm_num)
    have h := hLam.convolution
      (forwardCoeff_LSeries hW (s := 2) (by norm_num)).1
    exact h.abscissaOfAbsConv_le.trans_lt (EReal.coe_lt_top _)
  have hid : (fun x : ℝ => LSeries
      (LSeries.convolution (WeilHerglotz.lamC lam) (forwardCoeff lam)) x) =ᶠ[atTop]
      fun x => LSeries (LSeries.logMul (forwardCoeff lam)) x := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (1 : ℝ)] with x hx
    have hx' : 1 < (x : ℂ).re := by simpa using hx
    have hd := (hasDerivAt_LSeries_logZetaCoeff hH.summable (by simp) hx').cexp
    have heq : LSeries (forwardCoeff lam) =ᶠ[nhds (x : ℂ)]
        fun s => cexp (LSeries (logZetaCoeff (fun n => if 2 ≤ n then lam n else 0)) s) := by
      filter_upwards [isOpen_lt continuous_const continuous_re |>.mem_nhds hx'] with s hs
      exact (forwardCoeff_LSeries hW hs).2
    have hd' := hd.congr_of_eventuallyEq heq
    have hd'' := LSeries_hasDerivAt (s := (x : ℂ))
      (ha.trans_lt (by exact_mod_cast hx'))
    have hv := hd'.unique hd''
    rw [LSeries_convolution' (WeilHerglotz.summable_term_lamC hW hx')
      (forwardCoeff_LSeries hW hx').1, (forwardCoeff_LSeries hW hx').2]
    change LSeries (fun n => ((if 2 ≤ n then lam n else 0 : ℝ) : ℂ)) x *
      cexp (LSeries (logZetaCoeff (fun n => if 2 ≤ n then lam n else 0)) x) = _
    rw [mul_comm]
    exact neg_injective (by simpa only [mul_neg] using hv)
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
  · simp
  · have h := LSeries.eq_of_LSeries_eventually_eq hconv hlog hid hn.ne'
    simpa only [LSeries.logMul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast,
      Complex.ofReal_log (Nat.cast_nonneg n)] using h

/-- Raising a spectral penalty pointwise raises the optimal value. -/
theorem monotone_paperObservedGammaValue
    (c : ComplexNullMixture) (F : ι → ℝ →ᵇ ℂ) :
    Monotone (paperObservedGammaValue c F) := by
  intro G H hGH
  calc
    _ ≤ paperPerturbedGammaExpectation G (paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F H).1 :=
      paperObservedGammaValue_le c F G _
    _ ≤ paperPerturbedGammaExpectation H (paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F H).1 := by
      have hi := integral_mono
        (G.integrable ((paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F H).1 : Measure ℝ))
        (H.integrable ((paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F H).1 : Measure ℝ)) (fun ξ => hGH ξ)
      dsimp only [paperPerturbedGammaExpectation]
      linarith
    _ = _ := rfl

/-- Constant spectral penalties shift every probability-law objective by the same constant. -/
theorem paperPerturbedGammaExpectation_add_const
    (μ : ProbabilityMeasure ℝ) (G : ℝ →ᵇ ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
    paperPerturbedGammaExpectation (G + BoundedContinuousFunction.const ℝ a) μ =
      paperPerturbedGammaExpectation G μ + a := by
  unfold paperPerturbedGammaExpectation
  change (∫ ξ, paperSpectralGammaWeight ξ ∂(μ : Measure ℝ)) +
    (∫ ξ, G ξ + a ∂(μ : Measure ℝ)) = _
  rw [integral_add (G.integrable _) (integrable_const a), integral_const, probReal_univ, one_smul]
  ring

/-- The variational perturbation bound is attained for constant shifts. -/
theorem paperObservedGammaValue_add_const
    (c : ComplexNullMixture) (F : ι → ℝ →ᵇ ℂ) (G : ℝ →ᵇ ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
    paperObservedGammaValue c F (G + BoundedContinuousFunction.const ℝ a) =
      paperObservedGammaValue c F G + a := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · calc
      _ ≤ paperPerturbedGammaExpectation (G + BoundedContinuousFunction.const ℝ a)
          (paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F G).1 := paperObservedGammaValue_le c F _ _
      _ = _ := paperPerturbedGammaExpectation_add_const _ G a
  · have h := paperObservedGammaValue_le c F G
      (paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F (G + BoundedContinuousFunction.const ℝ a))
    have he : paperObservedGammaValue c F (G + BoundedContinuousFunction.const ℝ a) =
        paperPerturbedGammaExpectation G
          (paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F (G + BoundedContinuousFunction.const ℝ a)).1 + a :=
      paperPerturbedGammaExpectation_add_const _ G a
    linarith

/-- At a fixed law, the perturbed objective is affine in the bounded spectral penalty. -/
theorem paperPerturbedGammaExpectation_segment
    (μ : ProbabilityMeasure ℝ) (G H : ℝ →ᵇ ℝ) (t : Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    paperPerturbedGammaExpectation (t.1 • G + (1 - t.1) • H) μ =
      t.1 * paperPerturbedGammaExpectation G μ +
        (1 - t.1) * paperPerturbedGammaExpectation H μ := by
  unfold paperPerturbedGammaExpectation
  change (∫ ξ, paperSpectralGammaWeight ξ ∂(μ : Measure ℝ)) +
    (∫ ξ, t.1 * G ξ + (1 - t.1) * H ξ ∂(μ : Measure ℝ)) = _
  rw [integral_add ((G.integrable _).const_mul _) ((H.integrable _).const_mul _),
    integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul]
  ring

/-- The minimum gamma value is concave in the spectral penalty. -/
theorem paperObservedGammaValue_concave
    (c : ComplexNullMixture) (F : ι → ℝ →ᵇ ℂ) (G H : ℝ →ᵇ ℝ) (t : Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    t.1 * paperObservedGammaValue c F G + (1 - t.1) * paperObservedGammaValue c F H ≤
      paperObservedGammaValue c F (t.1 • G + (1 - t.1) • H) := by
  let μ := paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F (t.1 • G + (1 - t.1) • H)
  calc
    _ ≤ t.1 * paperPerturbedGammaExpectation G μ.1 +
        (1 - t.1) * paperPerturbedGammaExpectation H μ.1 :=
      add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (paperObservedGammaValue_le c F G μ) t.2.1)
        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (paperObservedGammaValue_le c F H μ)
          (sub_nonneg.mpr t.2.2))
    _ = paperPerturbedGammaExpectation (t.1 • G + (1 - t.1) • H) μ.1 :=
      (paperPerturbedGammaExpectation_segment μ.1 G H t).symm
    _ = _ := rfl

  have hv := paperObservedGammaValue_le_add_norm c F H G
  rw [norm_sub_rev] at hv
  have he : paperObservedGammaValue c F H =
      paperPerturbedGammaExpectation H (paperObservedGammaMinimizer c F H).1 := rfl
  constructor <;> linarith

          refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (by norm_num)
          calc Cm * (2 * T) ^ (1 - δ) ≤ max Cm 0 * (2 * T) ^ (1 - δ) :=
                mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (le_max_left _ _) (by positivity)
            _ ≤ max Cm 0 * (2 * T ^ (1 - δ)) :=
                mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h2 (le_max_right _ _)
      _ = max Cm 0 * T ^ (1 - δ) := by ring


/-- **Approximately integer spectral counting forces `Λ` and RH (mixed spectra).**  Let `lam` be
full-cone Weil-positive with boundary measure = integer atoms + real atoms `c_k` at `u_k` + a
positive rest `ν`, the diffuse part `Φ_d` of the Weil continuation being continuous up to the line.
The spectral phase is `θ(y) = 2π Σ_{u_k<y} c_k + 2∫_{−y}^{0} Re Φ_d(½+iv) dv`, i.e. `2π` times the
non-integer spectral mass below `y`.  If `e^{iθ(y)}` settles to a constant at a power rate in mean,
`∫_Y^{2Y} |e^{iθ(y)} − e^{2πiθ₀}| dy = O(Y^{1−δ})`, then `lam = Λ` and RH holds.

This is the approximate form of integer-counting rigidity
(`vonMangoldt_and_riemannHypothesis_of_integer_counting`). -/
theorem vonMangoldt_and_riemannHypothesis_of_settled_mixed_phase {lam : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) {m : ℕ → ℕ} {t c u : ℕ → ℝ} (hone : ∀ j, 1 ≤ t j)
    (hsum : Summable fun j => (m j : ℝ) / t j ^ 2) (hc : ∀ k, 0 ≤ c k) (hu1 : ∀ k, 1 ≤ u k)
    (hut : Tendsto u atTop atTop) (hcs2 : Summable fun k => c k / u k ^ 2) {ν : Measure ℝ}
    (hrep : ∀ w : ℂ, 0 < w.re → ∫⁻ r, poissonDensity w r ∂boundaryMeasure hW =
      (∑' j, ENNReal.ofReal (m j) * (poissonDensity w (t j) + poissonDensity w (-(t j)))) +
      (∑' k, ENNReal.ofReal (c k) * (poissonDensity w (u k) + poissonDensity w (-(u k)))) +
      ∫⁻ r, poissonDensity w r ∂ν)
    {Φd : ℂ → ℂ} (hΦdc : ContinuousOn Φd {s : ℂ | 1 / 2 ≤ s.re})
    (hΦdeq : ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 2 < s.re → weilContinuation hW s =
      atomicPairSeries (fun j => Real.pi * m j) t s +
        (∑' k, (c k : ℂ) * (2 * (s - 1 / 2) / ((s - 1 / 2) ^ 2 + (u k : ℂ) ^ 2))) + Φd s)
    {θ₀ δ Cm Y₁ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hsettle : ∀ Y : ℝ, Y₁ ≤ Y → ∫ y in Ioc Y (2 * Y),
      ‖cexp (((2 * Real.pi * phaseSum c u y +
          2 * ∫ v in -y..0, (Φd ((1 / 2 : ℂ) + (v : ℂ) * I)).re : ℝ) : ℂ) * I) -
        cexp (((2 * Real.pi * θ₀ : ℝ) : ℂ) * I)‖ ≤ Cm * Y ^ (1 - δ)) :
    (∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → lam n = ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n) ∧ RiemannHypothesis := by
  obtain ⟨hΦdd, hΦdre, hid⟩ := mixed_spectrum_data hW hone hsum hc hu1 hcs2 hrep hΦdeq
  obtain ⟨Φ, G, hΦd, -, hidΦ, hGc, hGd', hG2, hlock⟩ :=
    exists_producer_of_mixed_spectrum hone hsum hc hu1 hut hcs2 hΦdd hΦdc hΦdre hid
  have hGd : ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 2 < s.re → HasDerivAt G (weilContinuation hW s * G s) s := by
    intro s hs
    rw [← eqOn_weilContinuation hW hΦd hidΦ hs]
    exact hGd' s hs
  -- the phase
  set I₀ : ℝ → ℝ := fun y => ∫ v in -y..0, (Φd ((1 / 2 : ℂ) + (v : ℂ) * I)).re with hI₀
  have hcontΦ : Continuous fun v : ℝ => (Φd ((1 / 2 : ℂ) + (v : ℂ) * I)).re := by
    refine Complex.continuous_re.comp (hΦdc.comp_continuous (by fun_prop) fun v => ?_)
    show (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ ((1 / 2 : ℂ) + (v : ℂ) * I).re
    simp
  have hI₀c : Continuous I₀ := by
    have h := intervalIntegral.continuous_primitive (μ := volume)
      (fun a b => hcontΦ.intervalIntegrable a b) 0

cient (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (a : H) : ℂ :=
  (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ * Matrix.trace (grading * gram J a)

@[simp]
theorem gram_zero_zero
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (a : H) :
    gram J a 0 0 = ((‖a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  simp [gram, packet, Matrix.gram_apply, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]

@[simp]
theorem gram_zero_one
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (hJ : Function.Involutive J) (a : H) :
    gram J a 0 1 = Complex.I * (quadratic J a : ℂ) := by
  change inner ℂ a (Complex.I • J a) = _
  rw [inner_smul_right,
    ← inner_map_left_eq_inner_map_right J hJ a a,
    inner_map_self_eq_quadratic J hJ a]

@[simp]
theorem gram_one_zero
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (hJ : Function.Involutive J) (a : H) :
    gram J a 1 0 = -Complex.I * (quadratic J a : ℂ) := by
  change inner ℂ (Complex.I • J a) a = _
  rw [inner_smul_left, inner_map_self_eq_quadratic J hJ a]
  simp

@[simp]
theorem gram_one_one
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (a : H) :
    gram J a 1 1 = ((‖a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  change inner ℂ (Complex.I • J a) (Complex.I • J a) = _
  have hI : (starRingEnd ℂ) Complex.I * Complex.I = 1 := by
    rw [Complex.conj_I]
    simp [Complex.I_mul_I]
  rw [inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, J.inner_map_map, ← mul_assoc, hI, one_mul]
  simp [inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]

/-- Closed form of the Clifford Gram matrix. -/
theorem gram_eq
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (hJ : Function.Involutive J) (a : H) :
    gram J a =
      !![((‖a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ), Complex.I * (quadratic J a : ℂ);
        -Complex.I * (quadratic J a : ℂ), ((‖a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ)] := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [gram_zero_zero, gram_zero_one,
    gram_one_zero, gram_one_one, hJ]

/-- Matrix positivity is unconditional: it is Gram positivity, not Weil positivity. -/
theorem gram_posSemidef
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (a : H) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef (gram J a) :=
  Matrix.posSemidef_gram ℂ _

/-- The Clifford-graded coefficient of the positive lift is exactly the original quadratic form. -/
theorem coefficient_eq_quadratic
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (hJ : Function.Involutive J) (a : H) :
    coefficient J a = (quadratic J a : ℂ) := by
  rw [coefficient, gram_eq J hJ a]
  simp [grading, Matrix.trace_fin_two]
  linear_combination (-(quadratic J a : ℂ)) * Complex.I_mul_I

/-- Positive-channel energy identity. -/
theorem plus_channel_energy_eq
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (hJ : Function.Involutive J) (a : H) :
    ‖a + J a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) / 2 = ‖a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) + quadratic J a := by
  have hinner : RCLike.re (inner ℂ a (J a)) = quadratic J a := by
    rw [← inner_map_left_eq_inner_map_right J hJ a a]
    rfl
  rw [norm_add_sq (𝕜 := ℂ), J.norm_map, hinner]
  ring

/-- Negative-channel energy identity. -/
theorem minus_channel_energy_eq
    (J : H →ₗᵢ[ℂ] H) (hJ : Function.Involutive J) (a : H) :
    ‖a - J a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) / 2 = ‖a‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) - quadratic J a := by
  have hinner : RCLike.re (inner ℂ a (J a)) = quadratic J a := by
    rw [← inner_map_left_eq_inner_map_right J hJ a a]
    rfl
  rw [norm_sub_sq (𝕜 := ℂ), J.norm_map, hinner]
  ring

/-!
# The finite Gram--Weil block defect

This file isolates the finite-dimensional linear-algebra core of the
post-Gaussian Gram--Weil program.  It assumes only two finite-dimensional
Hilbert spaces and an injective linear map `C`; no Krein--Langer
factorization, model-space realization, or statement about the xi function
is assumed.

For

`G = [[I, -C], [-C†, I]]` and `J = [[I, 0], [0, -I]]`,

their defect is

`D = G - J = [[0, -C], [-C†, 2I]]`.

We define the positive and negative indices directly as the maximal
dimensions of subspaces on which the real quadratic form is strictly
positive or strictly negative.  The null index is the dimension of the
operator kernel.  This avoids taking an undeclared spectral-inertia API for
granted.
-/

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

open scoped ComplexConjugate

/-! ## An explicit, basis-free definition of finite quadratic inertia -/

/-- A real-valued quadratic function is strictly negative on a subspace. -/
def QuadraticStrictlyNegativeOn
    {𝕜 V : Type*} [DivisionRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕜 V]
    (q : V → ℝ) (W : Submodule 𝕜 V) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : W, x ≠ 0 → q x < 0

/-- A real-valued quadratic function is strictly positive on a subspace. -/
def QuadraticStrictlyPositiveOn
    {𝕜 V : Type*} [DivisionRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕜 V]
    (q : V → ℝ) (W : Submodule 𝕜 V) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : W, x ≠ 0 → 0 < q x

/-- `k` is the negative index when a `k`-dimensional negative-definite
subspace exists and every negative-definite subspace has dimension at most
`k`. -/
def HasQuadraticNegativeIndex
    {𝕜 V : Type*} [DivisionRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕜 V]
    (q : V → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∃ W : Submodule 𝕜 V,
      Module.finrank 𝕜 W = k ∧ QuadraticStrictlyNegativeOn q W) ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule 𝕜 V,
      QuadraticStrictlyNegativeOn q W → Module.finrank 𝕜 W ≤ k

/-- Positive-index analogue of `HasQuadraticNegativeIndex`. -/
def HasQuadraticPositiveIndex
    {𝕜 V : Type*} [DivisionRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕜 V]
    (q : V → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∃ W : Submodule 𝕜 V,
      Module.finrank 𝕜 W = k ∧ QuadraticStrictlyPositiveOn q W) ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule 𝕜 V,
      QuadraticStrictlyPositiveOn q W → Module.finrank 𝕜 W ≤ k

/-- Basis-free finite inertia, in `(negative, null, positive)` order. -/
def HasQuadraticInertia
    {𝕜 V : Type*} [DivisionRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕜 V]
    (operator : V →ₗ[𝕜] V) (q : V → ℝ)
    (negative null positive : ℕ) : Prop :=
  HasQuadraticNegativeIndex (𝕜 := 𝕜) q negative ∧
    Module.finrank 𝕜 operator.ker = null ∧
      HasQuadraticPositiveIndex (𝕜 := 𝕜) q positive

/-! ## The Gram--Weil defect operator and form -/

variable {𝕜 P N : Type*}
  [RCLike 𝕜]
  [NormedAddCommGroup P] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 P]
  [NormedAddCommGroup N] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 N]
  [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 P] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 N]

/-- The block operator `[[0, -C], [-C†, 2I]]`. -/
def gramWeilBlockDefectOperator (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P) :
    P × N →ₗ[𝕜] P × N where
  toFun x := (-C x.2, -C.adjoint x.1 + (2 : 𝕜) • x.2)
  map_add' x y := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> simp [add_assoc, add_left_comm, add_comm]
  map_smul' a x := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> simp [smul_add, smul_smul, mul_comm]

/-- The real quadratic form of `gramWeilBlockDefectOperator`. -/
def gramWeilBlockDefectQuadratic (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P)
    (x : P × N) : ℝ :=
  2 * ‖x.2‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) -
    2 * RCLike.re (inner 𝕜 x.2 (C.adjoint x.1))

/-- Completing the square in the negative block. -/
theorem gramWeilBlockDefectQuadratic_eq_completedSquare
    (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P) (x : P × N) :
    gramWeilBlockDefectQuadratic C x =
      (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ‖(2 : 𝕜) • x.2 - C.adjoint x.1‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) -
        (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ‖C.adjoint x.1‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
  unfold gramWeilBlockDefectQuadratic
  rw [norm_sub_sq (𝕜 := 𝕜), norm_smul]
  rw [inner_smul_left]
  norm_num [map_mul]
  ring

/-! ## The two control maps for the completed square -/

/-- The coordinate controlling negative directions. -/
def gramWeilNegativeControl (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P) :
    P × N →ₗ[𝕜] N :=
  C.adjoint.comp (LinearMap.fst 𝕜 P N)

/-- The completed-square coordinate controlling positive directions. -/
def gramWeilPositiveControl (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P) :
    P × N →ₗ[𝕜] N :=
  (2 : 𝕜) • LinearMap.snd 𝕜 P N -
    C.adjoint.comp (LinearMap.fst 𝕜 P N)

@[simp] theorem gramWeilNegativeControl_apply
    (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P) (x : P × N) :
    gramWeilNegativeControl C x = C.adjoint x.1 := rfl

@[simp] theorem gramWeilPositiveControl_apply
    (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P) (x : P × N) :
    gramWeilPositiveControl C x =
      (2 : 𝕜) • x.2 - C.adjoint x.1 := rfl

theorem gramWeilBlockDefectQuadratic_nonnegative_of_negativeControl_eq_zero
    (C : N →ₗ[𝕜] P) {x : P × N}
    (hx : gramWeilNegativeControl C x = 0) :
    0 ≤ gramWeilBlockDefectQuadratic C x := by
  rw [gramWeilBlockDefectQuadratic_eq_completedSquare]
  rw [gramWeilNegativeControl_apply] at hx

/-!
# Unconditional Hilbert realization of the Xi Weil form

Critical-line reflection permutes the multiplicity-exact Xi divisor.  Reindexing an `ell^(2 : ℕ)`
evaluation vector by this permutation realizes the Weil polarization as an ordinary Hilbert inner
product without assuming RH.  The reindexing preserves the norm, so the zero-side Weil form is a
bounded Hermitian form on its complete square-summable evaluation carrier.

This is the continuity bridge needed to pass positivity from an algebraic source-generated core to
its Hilbert closure.  It does not assert that the regular Cauchy core is dense in every divisor
evaluation vector; detecting the finite off-real sign vectors remains the top-down density problem.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Critical-line reflection acting on the multiplicity-exact Xi `ell^(2 : ℕ)` carrier. -/
def xiWeilLineConjLp (v : lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2) :
    lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2 :=
  ⟨fun q => v (xiZeroCopyLineConjEquiv q),
    HilbertSchmidt.memℓp_of_sq
      (xiZeroCopyLineConjEquiv.summable_iff.mpr
        (HilbertSchmidt.summable_coe_sq v))⟩

@[simp] theorem xiWeilLineConjLp_apply
    (v : lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2) (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    xiWeilLineConjLp v q = v (xiZeroCopyLineConjEquiv q) := rfl

/-- Critical-line reflection preserves the `ell^(2 : ℕ)` norm unconditionally. -/
theorem norm_xiWeilLineConjLp (v : lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2) :
    ‖xiWeilLineConjLp v‖ = ‖v‖ := by
  have hsq : ‖xiWeilLineConjLp v‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) = ‖v‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
    rw [HilbertSchmidt.lp_norm_sq_eq, HilbertSchmidt.lp_norm_sq_eq]
    exact xiZeroCopyLineConjEquiv.tsum_eq (fun q => ‖v q‖ ^ (2 : ℕ))
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (xiWeilLineConjLp v), norm_nonneg v]

/-- Critical-line reflection as a linear isometry of the Xi `ell^(2 : ℕ)` carrier. -/
def xiWeilLineConjLinearIsometry :
    lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2 →ₗᵢ[ℂ] lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2 where
  toFun := xiWeilLineConjLp
  map_add' v w := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext q
    rfl
  map_smul' c v := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    funext q
    rfl
  norm_map' := norm_xiWeilLineConjLp

@[simp] theorem xiWeilLineConjLinearIsometry_apply
    (v : lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2) :
    xiWeilLineConjLinearIsometry v = xiWeilLineConjLp v := rfl

/-- The real quadratic form carried by critical-line reflection on the Xi `ell^(2 : ℕ)` space. -/
def xiWeilHilbertQuadratic (v : lp (fun _ : XiZeroCopy => ℂ) 2) : ℝ :=
  (inner ℂ (xiWeilLineConjLinearIsometry v) v).re

/-- The unconditional Xi Hilbert quadratic form is continuous. -/
theorem continuous_xiWeilHilbertQuadratic : Continuous xiWeilHilbertQuadratic := by
  unfold xiWeilHilbertQuadratic
  fun_prop

/-- Positivity on the algebraic regular-Cauchy core automatically extends to its Hilbert closure. -/
theorem xiWeilHilbertQuadratic_nonneg_on_cauchyHilbertSubspace
    (hpos : ∀ v ∈ xiWeilCauchyAlgebraicSubspace, 0 ≤ xiWeilHilbertQuadratic v) :
    ∀ v ∈ xiWeilCauchyHilbertSubspace, 0 ≤ xiWeilHilbertQuadratic v := by
  intro v hv
  have hclosed : IsClosed {w | 0 ≤ xiWeilHilbertQuadratic w} :=
    isClosed_Ici.preimage continuous_xiWeilHilbertQuadratic
  have hv' : v ∈ closure (↑xiWeilCauchyAlgebraicSubspace : Set _) := by
    change v ∈ closure (↑xiWeilCauchyAlgebraicSubspace : Set _) at hv
    exact hv
  exact (closure_minimal hpos hclosed) hv'

/-- The Xi Weil polarization is the Hilbert product after critical-line-reflection reindexing.
No zero-location hypothesis is used. -/
theorem inner_xiWeilLineConjLp_evaluation_eq_polarization
    (F G : ℂ → ℂ) (hF : XiWeilSquareSummable F) (hG : XiWeilSquareSummable G) :
    inner ℂ (xiWeilLineConjLp (xiWeilEvaluationLp G hG))
      (xiWeilEvaluationLp F hF) = xiWeilPolarization F G := by
  rw [lp.inner_eq_tsum, xiWeilPolarization]
  apply tsum_congr
  intro q
  rw [xiWeilLineConjLp_apply, xiWeilEvaluationLp_apply,
    xiWeilEvaluationLp_apply, xiSpectralPoint_lineConj]
  simp [xiWeilSharp, RCLike.inner_apply]

/-- Evaluation identifies the continuous Hilbert quadratic form with the diagonal Weil value. -/
theorem xiWeilHilbertQuadratic_evaluation_eq_polarization_re
    (F : ℂ → ℂ) (hF : XiWeilSquareSummable F) :
    xiWeilHilbertQuadratic (xiWeilEvaluationLp F hF) =
      (xiWeilPolarization F F).re := by
  rw [xiWeilHilbertQuadratic, xiWeilLineConjLinearIsometry_apply,
    inner_xiWeilLineConjLp_evaluation_eq_polarization]

/-- Unconditional Cauchy--Schwarz bound for the Xi Weil polarization on square-summable tests. -/
theorem norm_xiWeilPolarization_le
    (F G : ℂ → ℂ) (hF : XiWeilSquareSummable F) (hG : XiWeilSquareSummable G) :
    ‖xiWeilPolarization F G‖ ≤
      ‖xiWeilEvaluationLp F hF‖ * ‖xiWeilEvaluationLp G hG‖ := by
  rw [← inner_xiWeilLineConjLp_evaluation_eq_polarization F G hF hG]
  calc
    ‖inner ℂ (xiWeilLineConjLp (xiWeilEvaluationLp G hG))

## Goal

Eliminate `xiRightTransverseSup` between the complete eighteen-chart aperture law and three
restricted-Weil floor growth laws. The resulting statement must transfer failure of one
geometric/analytic certificate into strict quantitative growth of a different observable.

**[PROVED HERE]** Fix positive `tau`, width `L`, and aperture `alpha`, with one admissible
negative-channel split and one nonnegative restricted-Weil floor envelope.

The Hedenmalm tail-cone equivalence, Xi half-plane-bound equivalence, and rectangular-Weil
transverse equivalence identify the full transverse certificate at `alpha` with

`xiRightTransverseSup ≤ alpha`.

If the certificate fails, therefore `alpha < xiRightTransverseSup`.

Under false RH, the restricted-Weil growth theorems give

`ofReal xiRightTransverseSup ≤ sampled upper logarithmic exponent`,

and

Strict monotonicity of the real embeddings into `ENNReal` and `EReal`, followed by transitivity,
replaces the intermediate transverse supremum by `alpha` in all three bounds. ∎
